purpose: Guide original series development and production; popularity is distinct from storytelling quality.

findings: DramaBox and ReelShort each approached $140M in Q1 2026 in-app revenue.
FreeReels ranked eighth among all apps by worldwide downloads that quarter.
High-emotion romance, revenge, fantasy, family conflict and status reversal recur; episodes use cliffhangers.
evidence.limits: IAP estimates are not total revenue or a ranking of artistic quality; region and monetization differ.

study_platforms.interpretation: A research shortlist, not a subjective quality ranking or recommendation to purchase subscriptions.

creative_hypotheses_not_proven_causality: Specific goals, injustice, longing and dramatic irony create an emotional reason to continue.
Each episode should change the situation, pay off something and open a consequential question.
A compelling ending must honor earlier setups rather than reset characters or rely on arbitrary twists.

product_defaults_not_industry_rules.note: Choose cuts around dramatic beats and speech. Current tested Wan profile generates about five seconds per take; do not stretch footage to pretend longer supported acting.

required_story_pipeline: Original premise, theme, central dramatic question and ending
Series bible with immutable character IDs, appearance/voice references, motivation, flaw, arc and relationships
Season/series beat map with causes, reversals, setups and scheduled payoffs
Ordered episode outlines with entry state, goal, conflict, turn, payoff, hook and exit state
Continuity validation against prior approved episodes: who knows what, secrets, relationships, injuries, wardrobe, props, location and story time
Storyboard/shot plan linked to characters, locations and narrative beats
Reference imagery, performances, dialogue and lip sync
Review, edit, sound, subtitles and export
Approve delivered episode and commit resulting canon; next episode starts from this state
acceptance_gates: Do not call a series coherent merely because documents are nonempty.
Later episodes must inherit the approved predecessor state and reuse character/voice identities.
A revised earlier episode invalidates dependent continuity approvals and identifies affected downstream work.
Every planned major setup has an intended payoff; finale resolves the central dramatic question.
Generated media must be checked against the screenplay and continuity, not just the immediately preceding prompt.
Autonomous orchestration must be resumable and distinguish proposed story changes from committed canon.
